marina.name: Marina, first-semester CS student
marina.studentStage: Beginner student taking introductory programming and web classes

goals.understandFirst: Understand what to study first without opening many disconnected resources
goals.shortExplanations: Find short explanations before committing to a full lesson
goals.mobileUse: Use the platform on a phone while commuting or between classes

needs.nextAction: Clear next study action after each topic

frustrations.unorderedTopics: Long lists of topics with no order

marina.scenario: Marina opens the platform before a study session, reads who Diogenes is, chooses a beginner track, and opens one topic to decide what to practice next.

navigationRelationships.homeLinks: Home introduces the purpose and links to Start Learning, Learning Tracks, and Accessibility Help.
navigationRelationships.startLearningRoute: Start Learning on Home and Learning Tracks opens the default student area tab at /tracks/history.
navigationRelationships.studentTabs: Learning Path History and Learning Path Builder are sibling tabs with URL-backed routes.
navigationRelationships.historyToBuilder: Learning Path History lists saved paths and links to /tracks/builder when students need a new path.
navigationRelationships.builderToLearning: Learning Path Builder lets students configure the current path and start or continue the saved path.
navigationRelationships.savedLearningSections: Saved learning paths open detailed learning sections and each section returns to the builder.
navigationRelationships.completionRoute: Completing the final topic opens a completion screen with a route back to /tracks/history.
navigationRelationships.tracksToTopics: Learning Tracks lists curated paths and links to foundation topic detail pages.
navigationRelationships.topicsToTracks: Topic pages explain one study unit and return students to Learning Tracks.
navigationRelationships.globalAccessibility: Accessibility Help is reachable from every main page through primary navigation.

contentHierarchy.pageHeading: Each page starts with one main heading and a short orientation paragraph.
contentHierarchy.repeatedItems: Repeated track and topic items use consistent labels and supporting descriptions.
contentHierarchy.studentSeparation: Student-area content separates history review from builder editing to reduce task switching confusion.
contentHierarchy.builderLayout: Builder content keeps the source catalog in a left tree and the current path in a main ordered view.
contentHierarchy.learningActions: Learning sections keep Complete Topic and Return to Builder actions before long markdown content.
contentHierarchy.primaryActions: Primary actions appear before secondary details on both desktop and mobile.

wireframeNotes.desktopHome: Desktop home uses a full-width professor image with overlayed introduction text and visible next-section preview.
wireframeNotes.mobileHome: Mobile home places the same introduction first, then stacks actions and content summaries.
wireframeNotes.trackOverview: Track overview uses repeated cards with title, purpose, recommendation, and topic links.
wireframeNotes.topicDetail: Topic detail uses a narrow reading column with key ideas and a next study action.
wireframeNotes.studentHistory: Student history uses a tab shell, then either an accessible table or an empty state with Add New Learning Path.
wireframeNotes.studentBuilder: Student builder uses a two-column desktop layout and stacks the action bar, catalog tree, and current path on mobile.
wireframeNotes.learningSection: Learning section pages use a constrained reading column so markdown tables, links, and lists stay readable.

visibilityOfStatus.finding: Students need to know which main area they are in while moving between Home, Tracks, and Accessibility Help.
visibilityOfStatus.iterationNote: Primary navigation includes current-page state and topic pages include return navigation.

recognition.finding: Track options should explain their purpose without requiring students to remember course terminology.
recognition.iterationNote: Each track includes a beginner-friendly summary, description, and recommended-for statement.

foundationAccessibility.finding: Students need keyboard navigation and a high-contrast option to use the foundation independently.
foundationAccessibility.iterationNote: The foundation includes skip link, focus states, semantic regions, and a high-contrast theme toggle.

userControl.finding: Students can make significant path edits and need a way to avoid losing or accidentally applying changes.
userControl.iterationNote: The builder separates Save from Continue Learning, disables invalid actions, and requires confirmation for discard and clear.

realWorldMatch.heuristic: Match between system and real world
realWorldMatch.finding: The builder must preserve the learning-track hierarchy so students do not see topics detached from their study context.
realWorldMatch.iterationNote: The current path groups selected topics under their parent track and only permits topic reordering inside that group.

errorPrevention.finding: Students may try to continue learning with unsaved edits or save an empty path.
errorPrevention.iterationNote: The action bar disables invalid actions and server actions return friendly feedback for blocked operations.

builderAccessibility.finding: The personalized builder introduces tabs, tree controls, context menus, dialogs, toasts, and long reading pages.
builderAccessibility.iterationNote: Student-area tabs expose selected state, controls have readable labels, destructive dialogs are explicit, and learning sections place Complete Topic before long content.
